days.guide: Write museum-style labels.

questions.q: What goes on a museum label?
questions.a: Artist name, title, date, medium, dimensions, and a short description.

days.guide: Plan the exhibition layout.

questions.a: By unit, medium, theme or chronology.

weeks.assessment_key: Curated portfolio rubric (1–4): 8–10 works representing every unit, mounted/matted neatly, museum labels (artist, title, date, medium, dimensions, 2–3 sentence description), logical layout plan. Proficient: all units represented and labels complete.

weeks.prep: Exhibition space, hooks/tape, the song, monologue and animation file, response cards, invitations to family/friends.
misconceptions: Hanging work too high. Hang 2-D art with the center at about eye level (around 57–60 inches).
Thinking only museums give art value. Context changes how art is viewed, but meaning comes from the work and its audience.

days.guide: Install the exhibition.

questions.q: At about what height should the center of a framed artwork hang?
questions.a: Eye level — about 57–60 inches from the floor.

days.guide: Rehearse song, monologue and gallery talk.

questions.a: A short talk explaining artworks to visitors.

days.guide: Host the showcase.

questions.q: Which work got the strongest reaction and why?
questions.a: Open answer.

days.guide: Collect visitor response cards.

questions.a: It is specific about what worked and what could change.

days.guide: Reflect on home vs museum viewing.

questions.q: How can location change how people value art?
questions.a: A museum setting suggests importance and expertise; home settings feel personal; lighting and labels affect attention.

weeks.assessment_key: Showcase rubric: exhibition installed neatly with labels; performances of a song, monologue and animation screening; gallery talk explains at least 3 works with vocabulary. Reflection proficient: compares home vs museum viewing (lighting, labels, scale, crowds, prestige, cost) and how location affects perceived value.

weeks.prep: Sketchbook, portfolio, camera/phone, slideshow app. Ideas for a summer sketchbook challenge (e.g., one drawing a day, 30-day prompts).
misconceptions: Measuring growth only by realism. Growth includes ideas, risk-taking, process and confidence.
Goals that are too vague. Make them specific and measurable.

days.guide: Compare first and last drawings; list three improved skills.

questions.q: Which skill improved most? Show evidence.
questions.a: Open answer — e.g., value range from 3 to 9 tones.

days.guide: Photograph all work; build a digital portfolio slideshow.

questions.q: Why photograph art in even, indirect light?
questions.a: To avoid glare and shadows and show true colors.

days.guide: Create one free-choice artwork.

questions.q: Which elements and principles did you use?
questions.a: Open answer — e.g., complementary colors and emphasis.

days.guide: Write a letter to your future self about your artistic identity.

questions.a: The interests, styles, subjects and values that make your art your own.

days.guide: Set goals for VAPA 8 and choose a summer challenge.

questions.a: Example: 'Fill 30 sketchbook pages with observational drawings by August 31.'

weeks.assessment_key: Digital portfolio rubric: photos of all major works, organized by unit, with titles and short reflections. Reflection letter proficient: names favorite medium and why, describes 3 skills that improved with evidence, describes artistic identity (style, interests) and goals for next year.

WL.overview: Spanish 1A builds Novice Low to Novice Mid skills through daily listening, speaking, reading and writing in short, real-life chunks: greetings, calendar, descriptions, likes, school, food, family, town and plans. Use Spanish for routines (greetings, the date, weather) every day even if you are learning alongside your child; model, have your child repeat, then let them use it with you in a role-play. Check accents and agreement in writing but praise communication first in speaking, and keep 10 minutes of Conjuguemos/Duolingo practice most days. Answers below give the correct Spanish so you can check even without fluency.

weeks.prep: Spanish notebook, a mirror for pronunciation, a free Duolingo account. Find a short greeting dialogue video (e.g., a Spanish Proficiency Exercises or Señor Jordan clip). Practice the vowel sounds a, e, i, o, u yourself.
misconceptions: Using 'buenos días' all day. Buenos días = morning (until about noon/lunch), buenas tardes = afternoon/early evening, buenas noches = night (also a goodnight).
Answering 'Mucho gusto' with 'Mucho gusto' only. That's fine, but 'Igualmente' (likewise) or 'El gusto es mío' are natural replies.

days.guide: Watch the dialogue, then say each greeting aloud and label a chart: morning → buenos días, afternoon → buenas tardes, night → buenas noches.

questions.q: Which greeting do you use at 3:00 p.m.?
questions.a: Buenas tardes.

questions.q: Which greeting do you use at 9:00 p.m.?
questions.a: Buenas noches.

days.guide: You play a new classmate. Practice: —¿Cómo te llamas? —Me llamo ___. ¿Y tú? —Me llamo ___. —Mucho gusto. —Igualmente. Record twice.

questions.q: How do you say 'My name is Ana'?
questions.a: Me llamo Ana.

questions.q: Someone says 'Mucho gusto.' What can you answer?
questions.a: Igualmente (or Mucho gusto / El gusto es mío).

days.guide: Learn farewells; your child writes and acts three 4-line dialogues that start with a greeting and end with a farewell.

questions.q: How do you say 'See you tomorrow'?
questions.a: Hasta mañana.
See you (later).

days.guide: Read about greeting customs; make a two-column chart comparing them with your family's.

questions.q: How do many people greet friends in Spain and much of Latin America?
questions.a: With a kiss on the cheek (one cheek in most of Latin America, two in Spain), or a handshake in formal settings.

days.guide: Finish Duolingo unit 1; do an unscripted greet–introduce–farewell exchange scored with the checklist.

questions.q: Translate: 'Good morning. My name is Luis. See you later.'
questions.a: Buenos días. Me llamo Luis. Hasta luego.

weeks.assessment_key: Oral exchange checklist (1 point each): greets appropriately for the time of day (Hola / Buenos días / Buenas tardes), asks or answers '¿Cómo te llamas?' with 'Me llamo…', responds to 'Mucho gusto' with 'Igualmente' or 'Mucho gusto', uses a farewell (Adiós / Hasta luego / Hasta mañana / Nos vemos). 4/4 = proficient; pronunciation intelligible.

weeks.prep: Draw emoji feeling cards (happy, tired, sick, so-so) and 12 index cards with people (best friend, grandmother, doctor, teacher, cousin, little brother, store clerk, principal, neighbor, pet, police officer, classmate). Find a UT Austin 'Spanish Proficiency Exercises' greeting clip.
misconceptions: Saying 'Estoy bueno' for 'I'm good.' Say 'Estoy bien' (bien is an adverb and doesn't change).
Using tú with adults you don't know. Use usted with elders, strangers, doctors and teachers; tú with friends, family your age and children.

days.guide: Draw a card; your child answers '¿Cómo estás?' to match: Muy bien / Bien / Regular / Así así / Mal / Estoy cansado(a).

questions.a: Estoy cansada.
So-so.

days.guide: Sort the 12 people into tú or usted and write a greeting for each (¿Cómo estás? vs ¿Cómo está usted?).

questions.q: Which form do you use with a doctor?
questions.a: Usted: ¿Cómo está usted?

questions.q: Which form do you use with your best friend?
questions.a: Tú: ¿Cómo estás?

days.guide: Watch the clip twice; note each speaker's name and feeling.

questions.q: If a speaker says 'Estoy un poco cansado,' how does he feel?
questions.a: A little tired.

days.guide: Role-play meeting an adult neighbor (usted) and a teammate (tú).

questions.q: Greet an older neighbor in the afternoon and ask how she is.
questions.a: Buenas tardes, señora. ¿Cómo está usted?

days.guide: Give the 15-item quiz and a 1-minute oral check-in.

questions.a: Bien, gracias. ¿Y tú? (or another feeling).

weeks.assessment_key: 15-item quiz: matching items like ¿Cómo estás? → Bien, gracias, ¿y tú?; ¿Cómo está usted? → Muy bien, gracias, ¿y usted?; ¿Cómo te llamas? → Me llamo…; ¿Qué tal? → Regular. Tú/usted: best friend tú, cousin tú, sibling tú, classmate tú, pet tú; grandmother usted (or tú in many families — accept either with reason), doctor usted, teacher usted, principal usted, store clerk usted, police officer usted, neighbor (adult) usted. 12/15 = 80% passing. Oral check-in: answers ¿Cómo estás? with a feeling and asks back with correct form.

weeks.prep: Alphabet chart, an alphabet song video, a deck of playing cards (remove face cards), dice. Write 8 dictation words (e.g., perro, llamar, niño, jugo, hola, gato, cero, quince).
misconceptions: Pronouncing h. Spanish h is silent: hola = 'OH-la'.
Mixing up 'veinte' style numbers: 16–19 and 21–29 are usually one word (dieciséis, veintiuno); 31 is three words (treinta y uno).

days.guide: Sing the alphabet; drill vowels a (ah), e (eh), i (ee), o (oh), u (oo); ñ (ny), ll (y), rr (trilled), j (h sound), h (silent).

questions.a: Like a strong English h: 'HOO-go'.
No — h is silent.

days.guide: Spell names aloud letter by letter; you write what you hear.

questions.q: How do you ask 'How do you spell it?'
questions.a: ¿Cómo se escribe?
a, ene, a.

days.guide: Learn 0–15; draw two cards and say the sum.

questions.a: Siete más ocho son quince.
Doce, catorce.

days.guide: Learn 16–31; dictate 15 phone-style strings (e.g., 'veinticinco–diecisiete–treinta').

questions.a: Veintidós, veintiséis.
Treinta y uno.

days.guide: Give the spelling dictation and number listening quiz.

weeks.assessment_key: Spelling dictation: 8 words spelled correctly including ñ, ll, rr and accents (7/8 proficient). Number quiz 0–31: cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez, once, doce, trece, catorce, quince, dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve, veinte, veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, veinticuatro, veinticinco, veintiséis, veintisiete, veintiocho, veintinueve, treinta, treinta y uno. 90% proficient.

weeks.prep: Blank world map, colored pencils, an online map game (e.g., Seterra 'Spanish-speaking countries'). Phone to record. List of California places: Los Ángeles, San Francisco, Sacramento, Fresno, Sierra Nevada, Monterey, etc.
misconceptions: Forgetting Equatorial Guinea. It is the one Spanish-speaking country in Africa.
Saying 'Soy en México' for 'I'm from Mexico.' Use 'Soy de México.'

days.guide: Label all 21 countries and capitals, color-coded by region.

questions.q: What is the capital of Argentina?
questions.a: Buenos Aires.

questions.q: Which Spanish-speaking country is in Africa, and what is its capital?
questions.a: Guinea Ecuatorial (Equatorial Guinea); capital Malabo.

days.guide: Practice —¿De dónde eres? —Soy de ___. List five California place names of Spanish origin.

questions.q: Give five California places with Spanish names.
questions.a: Los Ángeles, San Francisco, Sacramento, San Diego, Fresno, Sierra Nevada, Monterey, Santa Cruz (any five).

questions.q: Answer in Spanish: ¿De dónde eres? (from California)
questions.a: Soy de California.

days.guide: Drill the map game until all 21 can be placed in under 5 minutes.

questions.q: What is the capital of Peru? Of Colombia?
questions.a: Lima; Bogotá.

days.guide: Write and record a self-introduction.

questions.q: How do you say 'I am 12 years old'?
questions.a: Tengo doce años.

days.guide: Give the unit 1 test and collect the recording.

questions.q: Name the capital of Spain and of Mexico.
questions.a: Madrid; Ciudad de México.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 1 test: greetings listening (match greeting to time of day/feelings), numbers 0–31, alphabet spelling, and map. 21 countries and capitals: España–Madrid; México–Ciudad de México; Guatemala–Ciudad de Guatemala; Honduras–Tegucigalpa; El Salvador–San Salvador; Nicaragua–Managua; Costa Rica–San José; Panamá–Ciudad de Panamá; Cuba–La Habana; República Dominicana–Santo Domingo; Puerto Rico–San Juan; Colombia–Bogotá; Venezuela–Caracas; Ecuador–Quito; Perú–Lima; Bolivia–La Paz (seat of government) and Sucre (constitutional capital); Chile–Santiago; Argentina–Buenos Aires; Uruguay–Montevideo; Paraguay–Asunción; Guinea Ecuatorial–Malabo. Recording rubric: greeting, name, feeling, age (Tengo __ años), origin (Soy de…), farewell; 6/6 proficient with intelligible pronunciation.

weeks.prep: Printable calendar, markers, list of family birthdays. Read about 16 de septiembre, 12 de octubre and 6 de enero.
misconceptions: Capitalizing days and months. In Spanish they are lowercase: lunes, enero.
Saying 'el uno de enero.' The first of the month is 'el primero de enero'; other dates use cardinal numbers (el dos, el tres…).

days.guide: Learn days (week starts on lunes); write today/tomorrow statements.

questions.q: If today is Tuesday, write 'Today is Tuesday, tomorrow is Wednesday.'
questions.a: Hoy es martes, mañana es miércoles.

questions.q: Which day starts the week on Spanish calendars?
questions.a: Lunes (Monday).

days.guide: Learn the 12 months; fill a calendar with family events.

questions.a: agosto.

days.guide: Teach date format; write 10 family birthdays.

questions.a: El cumpleaños de mi mamá es el cinco de mayo.
el primero de enero.

days.guide: Read about three holidays; mark them.

questions.q: What is celebrated on el 16 de septiembre?
questions.a: Mexican Independence Day (Grito de Dolores, 1810).

questions.q: What is el Día de Reyes (6 de enero)?
questions.a: Three Kings Day (Epiphany), when children receive gifts and families eat rosca de reyes.

days.guide: Ask ¿Qué día es hoy? and ¿Cuál es la fecha? for five dates; give the written quiz.

questions.a: Es el doce de octubre.

weeks.assessment_key: Dates quiz: days lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo; months enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre. Sample items: 4/7 → el cuatro de julio; 1/1 → el primero de enero; 25/12 → el veinticinco de diciembre; 14/2 → el catorce de febrero. Format: day before month (el 5 de mayo). 80% proficient. Oral: answers '¿Qué día es hoy?' (Hoy es ___) and '¿Cuál es la fecha?' (Es el ___ de ___).

weeks.prep: Paper plate, brad fastener, construction paper hands. A daily schedule. Find a Spanish train timetable (Renfe) or TV listing with 24-hour times.
misconceptions: Saying 'son la una.' One o'clock is singular: Es la una; all other hours use son las…
Confusing ¿Qué hora es? (What time is it now?) with ¿A qué hora es…? (At what time is…?).

days.guide: Build the clock; practice es la una / son las dos, y cuarto, y media, menos diez.

questions.a: Son las dos y media.
Son las cuatro menos cuarto (or son las tres y cuarenta y cinco).

days.guide: Add de la mañana/tarde/noche; write times of 10 daily events.

questions.a: Como el almuerzo a las doce y media de la tarde.
Son las siete de la mañana.

days.guide: Contrast ¿Qué hora es? with ¿A qué hora es…?; ask five questions.

questions.q: Answer: ¿A qué hora es la cena? (6:00)
questions.a: La cena es a las seis.

days.guide: Read 24-hour times and convert them.

questions.q: A train leaves at 17:15. Say it in conversational Spanish.
questions.a: A las cinco y cuarto de la tarde.

days.guide: Give the listening quiz and oral clock reading.

questions.a: Es la una y diez.

weeks.assessment_key: Listening quiz: parent reads 10 times, child draws hands. Sample key: Es la una y cuarto (1:15); Son las tres y media (3:30); Son las cinco menos diez (4:50); Son las ocho y veinte (8:20); Es mediodía (12:00 p.m.). Oral: says 10 clock times correctly (8/10 proficient), using y for minutes after and menos for minutes before the hour (past :30).

weeks.prep: A Spanish-language weather site (e.g., AccuWeather en español, Meteored), world map, phone to record.
misconceptions: Using 'es' with weather. Use hace (hace calor), está (está nublado), or verbs llueve/nieva.
Thinking seasons are the same everywhere. Southern Hemisphere countries (Argentina, Chile, Uruguay) have summer in December–February.

days.guide: Learn weather expressions; give a daily report.

questions.q: How do you say 'It's hot and sunny'?
questions.a: Hace calor y hace sol.
Llueve (or Está lloviendo).

days.guide: Match months to seasons for California and Argentina; explain why reversed.

questions.q: What season is it in Argentina in January?
questions.a: Verano (summer).
Argentina is in the Southern Hemisphere, which tilts toward the sun when the Northern Hemisphere tilts away.

days.guide: Read forecasts for Mexico City and Buenos Aires; record temperature and conditions.

questions.a: It's cloudy.

days.guide: Write and record a 45-second weather report.

questions.q: Write: 'Today is Monday, March 3. In Madrid it is cold and windy.'
questions.a: Hoy es lunes, el tres de marzo. En Madrid hace frío y hace viento.

days.guide: Give the unit 2 test.

questions.q: Name the four seasons in Spanish.
questions.a: La primavera, el verano, el otoño, el invierno.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 2 test: days, months, dates, time, weather with listening. Seasons key: primavera, verano, otoño, invierno. California: invierno = diciembre–febrero, primavera = marzo–mayo, verano = junio–agosto, otoño = septiembre–noviembre; Argentina reversed (verano = diciembre–febrero). Weather report rubric: names 3 capitals, date and time, conditions and temperature in Spanish, 45 seconds, clear pronunciation.

weeks.prep: Pronoun chart, Conjuguemos account (free), 20 pictures of people (yourself, a friend, groups of boys/girls/mixed).
misconceptions: Using ellas for a mixed group. Any group with at least one male uses ellos/nosotros.
Always saying the subject pronoun. Spanish often drops it because the verb shows the subject: Soy de California.

days.guide: Teach pronouns; assign pronouns to 20 pictures.

questions.a: Ellos.
Ellas.

days.guide: Teach ser forms; Conjuguemos drill to 90%.

questions.q: Conjugate ser for nosotros and ellos.
questions.a: Somos; son.
eres.

days.guide: Write 10 origin sentences with ser de.

questions.a: Lionel Messi es de Argentina.
Somos de California.

days.guide: Ask/answer ¿Eres…? questions; practice negatives with no before the verb.

questions.a: No, no soy de España.

days.guide: Give the ser and pronoun quiz.

questions.q: Which pronoun is used for 'you all' in most of Latin America?
questions.a: Ustedes.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: ser — yo soy, tú eres, él/ella/usted es, nosotros/as somos, vosotros/as sois, ellos/ellas/ustedes son. Pronoun items: Ana → ella; Ana y yo → nosotras; Juan y María → ellos; you (formal) → usted; you all (Latin America) → ustedes; you all (Spain, informal) → vosotros. Sample sentences: Nosotros somos de Texas. ¿Tú eres de Chile? Ellas son de Perú. 80% passing.

weeks.prep: Flashcards for 16 adjectives: simpático, antipático, gracioso, serio, trabajador, perezoso, inteligente, paciente, impaciente, deportista, artístico, ordenado, desordenado, talentoso, tímido, sociable.
misconceptions: Using -o adjectives for girls. Feminine: simpática, seria; adjectives ending in -e or -ista don't change for gender (inteligente, deportista).
Putting adjectives before nouns like English. Most descriptive adjectives follow the noun: una chica simpática.

days.guide: Learn adjectives; describe self with soy / no soy.

questions.q: A girl says 'I am funny but not lazy.'
questions.a: Soy graciosa pero no soy perezosa.

days.guide: Teach -o/-a/-os/-as, -e → -es, consonant → -es (trabajador → trabajadora/trabajadores).

questions.a: Las chicas son serias.
Los chicos son inteligentes.

days.guide: Use muy, un poco, bastante and y/pero to describe three family members.

questions.q: Write: 'My dad is very hardworking and a little serious.'
questions.a: Mi papá es muy trabajador y un poco serio.

days.guide: Interview a parent with ¿Cómo eres? ¿Eres…?; write five sentences.

questions.q: Ask your mom if she is patient.
questions.a: ¿Eres paciente? (or formal: ¿Es usted paciente?)

days.guide: Give the agreement quiz; record a self-description.

questions.a: Mi hermana es trabajadora.

weeks.assessment_key: Agreement quiz key (sample): 1) Ella es (trabajador) → trabajadora 2) Ellos son (gracioso) → graciosos 3) Mis amigas son (inteligente) → inteligentes 4) Él es (deportista) → deportista 5) Nosotras somos (serio) → serias 6) Tú (a girl) eres (perezoso) → perezosa 7) Las chicas son (sociable) → sociables. 80% proficient. Oral self-description: 30 seconds with soy/no soy, 4+ adjectives with correct agreement.

weeks.prep: Magazine photos or printed images of people; famous-person cards. Nationality list: mexicano, español, argentino, colombiano, peruano, chileno, cubano, puertorriqueño, dominicano, venezolano, estadounidense, guatemalteco.
misconceptions: Using ser for hair and eyes. Use tener: Tiene el pelo castaño y los ojos azules.
Capitalizing nationalities. Nationalities are lowercase in Spanish: mexicana.

days.guide: Learn alto, bajo, rubio, moreno, pelirrojo, tiene el pelo / los ojos…; describe 6 photos.

questions.q: Write: 'She is tall and has brown eyes.'
questions.a: Ella es alta y tiene los ojos castaños (or marrones/cafés).
Él es pelirrojo (or tiene el pelo rojo).

days.guide: Teach definite and indefinite articles; sort 20 nouns.

questions.q: Give the definite and indefinite article for 'mochila'.
questions.a: la mochila, una mochila.
el (el día — an exception ending in -a).

days.guide: Learn 12 nationalities and agreement; write sentences about famous people.

questions.a: Shakira es colombiana.
españolas.

days.guide: Play guess-who with yes/no questions (¿Es alta? ¿Tiene el pelo rubio?).

questions.a: ¿Tiene los ojos azules?

days.guide: Give the reading quiz.

questions.q: What does 'Es mexicano, bajo y muy gracioso' mean?
questions.a: He is Mexican, short and very funny.

weeks.assessment_key: Reading quiz: matches four profiles to pictures (4/4 proficient). Articles key: el libro, la mesa, los chicos, las chicas, un perro, una casa, unos lápices, unas mochilas; el día and el mapa are masculine, la mano feminine. Nationality agreement: español/española/españoles/españolas; estadounidense (no gender change).

weeks.prep: Poster board or slides, library books or reliable sites, SpanishDict.com. Help choose a figure (Frida Kahlo, Lionel Messi, Sonia Sotomayor, Ellen Ochoa, Gabriel García Márquez, Selena, etc.).
misconceptions: Translating long English sentences word for word. Use structures you know: Es…, Tiene…, Es de…, Le gusta…
Reading the poster aloud. Present from key words to sound natural.

days.guide: Choose a figure; collect 5 facts and key Spanish words.

questions.q: How do you say 'She is a famous artist'?
questions.a: Es una artista famosa.

days.guide: Write an 8–10 sentence profile.

questions.q: Write: 'Ellen Ochoa is an American astronaut. She is intelligent.'
questions.a: Ellen Ochoa es una astronauta estadounidense. Es inteligente.

days.guide: Revise with checklist; look up three words.

questions.q: Find the error: 'Sonia Sotomayor es una juez importanta.'
questions.a: 'importanta' should be 'importante' (and 'juez' → 'jueza' is also accepted): Sonia Sotomayor es una jueza importante.

days.guide: Make the poster/slides; practice without reading.

questions.q: Why is 'el artista' / 'la artista' the same word?
questions.a: Nouns ending in -ista keep the same form; only the article shows gender.

days.guide: Present (1–2 minutes); give unit 3 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'Lionel Messi is Argentine, short and very hardworking.'
questions.a: Lionel Messi es argentino, bajo y muy trabajador.

weeks.assessment_key: Presentational rubric (1–4 each): content (8–10 sentences: name, nationality, origin, profession, personality, appearance, why important), language (ser, tener, agreement, articles), pronunciation/fluency, visuals. Unit 3 test: ser conjugation, pronouns, adjective agreement, nationalities, articles, physical description. Model sentence: Frida Kahlo es una artista mexicana. Es de Coyoacán, México. Es talentosa y fuerte. Tiene el pelo negro y los ojos castaños.

weeks.prep: Activity picture cards for 18 infinitives (nadar, bailar, cantar, dibujar, leer, escribir, montar en bicicleta, jugar videojuegos, practicar deportes, correr, tocar la guitarra, usar la computadora, ver la tele, escuchar música, patinar, cocinar, hablar por teléfono, pasar tiempo con amigos). A teen hobby podcast or video in Spanish (e.g., from a textbook site or YouTube).
misconceptions: Conjugating the activity after gustar: 'Me gusta nado.' Use the infinitive: Me gusta nadar.
Saying 'Yo gusto…' Use 'Me gusta…' (literally, it pleases me).

days.guide: Learn 18 activities; act them out for guessing.

questions.a: To ride a bike.
nadar.

days.guide: Write 10 sentences with me gusta / no me gusta / me gusta más.

questions.q: Write: 'I like to read but I don't like to write.'
questions.a: Me gusta leer pero no me gusta escribir.

days.guide: Ask a family member 10 ¿Te gusta…? questions; record answers.

questions.a: Sí, me gusta cocinar.

days.guide: Listen to two teens; note likes and dislikes.

questions.q: If you hear 'No me gusta nada correr,' what does it mean?
questions.a: I don't like running at all.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary and gustar quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'Do you like to play video games?'
questions.a: ¿Te gusta jugar videojuegos?

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz: vocabulary matching (18 activities) and sentences. Key samples: I like to dance → Me gusta bailar; I don't like to sing → No me gusta cantar; Do you like to read? → ¿Te gusta leer?; I like to draw more → Me gusta más dibujar. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Survey sheet, 15 statements to read aloud (Me gusta nadar, No me gusta cocinar…).
misconceptions: Answering a negative statement with 'a mí también.' Agree with a negative using 'a mí tampoco'; disagree with 'a mí sí.'
Saying 'Ella gusta…' Use 'A ella le gusta…'

days.guide: React to 15 statements: positive + agree → a mí también; positive + disagree → a mí no; negative + agree → a mí tampoco; negative + disagree → a mí sí.

questions.q: Statement: 'Me gusta nadar.' You also like it. React.
questions.a: A mí también.

questions.q: Statement: 'No me gusta correr.' You do like it. React.
questions.a: A mí sí.

days.guide: Report relatives' likes with a él/a ella le gusta.

questions.a: A mi abuela le gusta cocinar.

days.guide: Practice no…nada, ni…ni, tampoco in 10 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'I don't like to run or swim.'
questions.a: No me gusta ni correr ni nadar.

questions.q: Write: 'I don't like to do anything.'
questions.a: No me gusta hacer nada.

days.guide: Survey five people; graph results with Spanish labels.

questions.q: Ask: 'What do you like to do?'
questions.a: ¿Qué te gusta hacer?

days.guide: Hold a 2-minute conversation; give the writing check.

questions.q: Statement: 'No me gusta dibujar.' You don't either. React.
questions.a: A mí tampoco.

weeks.assessment_key: Conversation rubric (1–4): asks and answers about likes, reacts with también/tampoco/sí/no correctly, keeps going 2 minutes, comprehensibility. Writing check key samples: 'My brother likes to skate' → A mi hermano le gusta patinar; 'I don't like to sing or dance' → No me gusta ni cantar ni bailar; 'I don't either' → A mí tampoco.

weeks.prep: Culture reading about pastimes, a Señor Wooly video (free ones on senorwooly.com, e.g., '¿Puedo ir al baño?' or 'Billy la Bufanda'), a sample pen-pal email, Venn diagram.
misconceptions: Thinking all Spanish-speaking countries share the same favorite sport. Fútbol dominates most, but béisbol is huge in the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Venezuela and Puerto Rico.
Starting emails with 'Hola Querido.' Use 'Querido Juan:' / 'Querida Ana:' (colon), and close with 'Tu amigo/a' or 'Saludos'.

days.guide: Read about fútbol in Argentina, béisbol in the Dominican Republic, el paseo in Spain; list products and practices.

questions.a: An evening stroll through town or the plaza to socialize, common in Spain.

questions.q: Which sport is most popular in the Dominican Republic?
questions.a: Béisbol (baseball).

days.guide: Watch a Señor Wooly video; list activity words; summarize in English.

questions.q: Name two activity words you heard.
questions.a: Open answer — check they are actual verbs from the video.

days.guide: Write a 10-sentence pen-pal email.

questions.q: Write an opening for a letter to a girl named Sofía.
questions.a: Querida Sofía:

days.guide: Make a Venn diagram; write three comparison sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'In Mexico and in California people like soccer.'
questions.a: En México y en California a la gente le gusta el fútbol.

days.guide: Give the unit 4 test.

questions.a: A hobby/pastime.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 4 test: listening to likes, reading a pen-pal letter, writing a reply. Pen-pal email rubric (1–4): greeting (Querido/a…), introduces self (name, age, origin, personality), 3+ likes/dislikes with gustar, asks 3 questions (¿Qué te gusta hacer? ¿Te gusta…? ¿Cómo eres?), closing; accurate agreement. Proficient = 10 sentences with all parts.

weeks.prep: Sticky notes, 20 school supplies and furniture items. List of classroom commands: Saquen una hoja de papel, Repitan, Escuchen, Siéntense, Levántense, Abran el libro, Cierren el libro, Escriban, ¿Cómo se dice…?, ¿Qué quiere decir…?, Levanten la mano, Miren la pizarra.
misconceptions: Forgetting the z→c change in plurals: lápiz → lápices.
Using 'hay' with an article for specific things. Hay means there is/are with indefinite things: Hay un lápiz; Hay dos libros.

days.guide: Label 20 objects with el/la.

questions.q: Give the article: mochila, cuaderno, computadora, bolígrafo.
questions.a: la mochila, el cuaderno, la computadora, el bolígrafo.

days.guide: Teach plural rules: vowel + s; consonant + es; z → ces.

questions.q: Make plural: el lápiz, el papel, la regla.
questions.a: los lápices, los papeles, las reglas.

days.guide: Describe backpack and desk using hay + numbers.

questions.q: Write: 'In my backpack there are two notebooks and a pencil.'
questions.a: En mi mochila hay dos cuadernos y un lápiz.

days.guide: TPR game: you give commands; child acts them out.

questions.q: What does 'Saquen una hoja de papel' mean?
questions.a: Take out a sheet of paper.

questions.q: How do you ask 'How do you say 'eraser'?'
questions.a: ¿Cómo se dice 'eraser'?

days.guide: Give the quiz.

questions.a: Hay cuatro bolígrafos.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key samples: el lápiz → los lápices; el cuaderno → los cuadernos; la carpeta → las carpetas; el papel → los papeles; el reloj → los relojes; la computadora → las computadoras. Hay sentences: 'There are three folders in my backpack' → En mi mochila hay tres carpetas. ¿Cuántos libros hay? → Hay cinco libros. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Blank weekly schedule, price ads, bingo cards with numbers 32–100. Read about school in Mexico or Chile.
misconceptions: Writing 'treintaidos.' From 31 on, tens and units are separate words with y: treinta y dos.
Adjective agreement with subjects: 'las matemáticas son difíciles' (plural).

days.guide: Learn subjects and ordinals 1st–8th; fill a schedule.

questions.q: Say: 'In first period I have science.'
questions.a: En la primera hora tengo ciencias.
tercero/tercera (tercer before a masculine singular noun).

days.guide: Learn tens (treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa, cien); play bingo.

questions.a: setenta y seis.
cien.

days.guide: Write opinions about each subject.

questions.a: Las matemáticas son difíciles pero interesantes.

days.guide: Read about school in Mexico/Chile; list 4 differences.

questions.a: Recess/break.

days.guide: Interview and give the number dictation.

weeks.assessment_key: Schedule interview: answers ¿Qué clase tienes en la primera hora? (En la primera hora tengo matemáticas), ¿A qué hora es el almuerzo?, ¿Qué clase te gusta más? Ordinals: primero, segundo, tercero, cuarto, quinto, sexto, séptimo, octavo (primer/tercer before masculine nouns). Numbers dictation key: 32 treinta y dos, 45 cuarenta y cinco, 58 cincuenta y ocho, 67 sesenta y siete, 74 setenta y cuatro, 83 ochenta y tres, 96 noventa y seis, 100 cien. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Verb chart, Conjuguemos -ar practice. Verbs: hablar, estudiar, trabajar, usar, necesitar, enseñar, practicar, tocar, escuchar, bailar, cantar, nadar.
misconceptions: Leaving the -ar on: 'yo hablaro.' Drop -ar, add the ending: hablo.
Forgetting accents in vosotros: habláis.

days.guide: Teach infinitive, stem, endings; chart hablar and estudiar.

questions.q: Conjugate estudiar for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: estudio; estudiamos.
trabaj-.

days.guide: Conjuguemos drill to 90%; write 10 sentences.

questions.a: Practicamos fútbol.

days.guide: Describe family members' weekdays.

questions.q: Write: 'My mom works in the morning.'
questions.a: Mi mamá trabaja por la mañana.

days.guide: Form questions (¿Qué estudias? ¿Cuándo trabajas?); interview a parent.

questions.q: Ask: 'What do you need for class?'
questions.a: ¿Qué necesitas para la clase?
No, no toco la guitarra.

days.guide: Give the -ar quiz.

questions.a: escuchan.

weeks.assessment_key: -ar quiz: hablar → hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. Sample items: Nosotros (estudiar) → estudiamos; Ellos (trabajar) → trabajan; Tú (necesitar) → necesitas; Ella (enseñar) → enseña; Yo (tocar) → toco; Ustedes (usar) → usan. Sentence-writing: 5 sentences with correct subject-verb agreement. 80% passing.

weeks.prep: All semester tests, flashcards, a practice listening quiz (you read 10 items aloud), can-do checklist.
misconceptions: Cramming. Review a little each day with flashcards and say answers aloud.
Writing English sentence structure in Spanish. Use the patterns practiced: Me llamo…, Soy…, Me gusta…, Tengo…

days.guide: Review units 1–2 with flashcards and a practice listening quiz.

questions.q: Say the date and time: Wednesday, Nov 20, 3:15 p.m.
questions.a: Hoy es miércoles, el veinte de noviembre. Son las tres y cuarto de la tarde.

days.guide: Review units 3–5 with a practice test.

questions.q: Translate: 'My friends are funny and they like to dance.'
questions.a: Mis amigos son graciosos y les gusta bailar.

days.guide: 3-minute interview: name, origin, personality, likes, schedule.

questions.a: Soy ___ y ___ (two agreeing adjectives), e.g., Soy simpático y trabajador.

days.guide: Give the written exam.

questions.a: necesitamos.

days.guide: Complete a can-do checklist and set two goals.

questions.q: Write a Spanish goal in English or Spanish.
questions.a: Example: 'Practice Conjuguemos 10 minutes 4 days a week.'

weeks.assessment_key: Semester exam (suggested): Listening 10 pts (greetings, times, dates); Reading 10 (short profile with true/false); Grammar 20 (ser, adjective agreement, gustar, -ar verbs, plurals, hay); Writing 10 (10 sentences about self: name, age, origin, personality, likes, schedule, date) — rubric: content, accuracy, variety. Oral interview rubric (1–4): comprehension, answers in full sentences, asks a question back, pronunciation. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Grocery ads (Spanish ones if available), food pictures. Vocabulary: el pan, el pan tostado, los huevos, el tocino, la salchicha, el cereal, el yogur, la fruta, el plátano, la manzana, la leche, el jugo de naranja, el café; lunch: el sándwich, la hamburguesa, la pizza, la sopa, la ensalada, el queso, el jamón, las papas fritas, la galleta, el refresco, el agua, el té.
misconceptions: Saying 'me gusta las fresas.' With plural nouns use gustan: Me gustan las fresas.
Leaving out the article after gustar: Me gusta el jugo (not 'me gusta jugo').

days.guide: Learn 12 breakfast foods; label a picture of your breakfast.

questions.q: How do you say 'eggs' and 'orange juice'?
questions.a: los huevos; el jugo de naranja.

days.guide: Learn 12 lunch foods; sort into frutas, verduras, carnes, bebidas.

questions.q: Classify: la manzana, el jamón, la leche, la lechuga.
questions.a: fruta; carne; bebida; verdura.

days.guide: Teach gusta/gustan, encanta/encantan; write 10 sentences.

questions.a: Me encantan los plátanos.
gusta.

days.guide: Ask three family members ¿Qué comes en el desayuno?; summarize.

questions.q: Summarize: 'My dad eats eggs and toast.'
questions.a: Mi papá come huevos y pan tostado.

days.guide: Give the quiz.

questions.a: No me gustan las papas fritas.

weeks.assessment_key: Food vocabulary quiz: label 20 foods with articles; gustar/encantar: Me gustan los huevos; Me encanta la pizza; No me gustan las salchichas; ¿Te gusta el yogur? 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Verb chart, Conjuguemos -er/-ir practice.
misconceptions: Using -amos with -er/-ir verbs. -er → -emos (comemos); -ir → -imos (vivimos).
Mixing up siempre/nunca placement. 'Nunca como…' or 'No como nunca…'

days.guide: Teach -er endings; chart comer, beber, leer.

questions.q: Conjugate beber for tú and ellos.
questions.a: bebes; beben.

days.guide: Teach -ir endings (same as -er except nosotros -imos, vosotros -ís); chart vivir, escribir, compartir.

questions.a: escribimos.

questions.q: Which forms differ between -er and -ir verbs?
questions.a: Nosotros (-emos/-imos) and vosotros (-éis/-ís).

days.guide: Drill to 90%; write 10 sentences with siempre, a veces, nunca.

questions.a: Nunca bebo café.

days.guide: Interview a parent: eight questions with -er/-ir verbs.

questions.q: Ask: 'What do you eat for lunch?'
questions.a: ¿Qué comes en el almuerzo?

days.guide: Give the -ar/-er/-ir quiz.

questions.q: Conjugate leer for nosotros and compartir for ella.
questions.a: leemos; comparte.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: comer — como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen; vivir — vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven. Sample items: Yo (beber) → bebo; Nosotros (escribir) → escribimos; Ellas (leer) → leen; Tú (compartir) → compartes; Nosotros (comprender) → comprendemos; Ustedes (vivir) → viven; Mi hermano (hablar) → habla. 80% passing.

weeks.prep: MyPlate graphic, a Spanish nutrition label (información nutricional — many U.S. products have bilingual labels), short healthy-eating article in Spanish. Vocabulary: las verduras, las zanahorias, la lechuga, los tomates, los guisantes, las judías verdes, el pollo, el pescado, la carne de res, el arroz, los frijoles, la grasa.
misconceptions: Agreement with plural foods: 'Las zanahorias son sabrosas' (not sabroso).
Using 'debe' with a conjugated verb. Deber + infinitive: Debes comer verduras.

days.guide: Learn 12 vegetable/protein words; classify bueno/malo para la salud.

questions.q: Is 'el pescado' bueno or malo para la salud?
questions.a: Bueno para la salud.

days.guide: Describe 10 foods with ser + agreeing adjectives.

questions.a: Los guisantes son horribles.
El pollo es sabroso.

days.guide: Read a Spanish nutrition label; answer about grasa, azúcar, calorías.

questions.a: Total fat.
Added sugars.

days.guide: Draw a balanced plate; write 6 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'To stay healthy you should eat vegetables.'
questions.a: Para mantener la salud debes comer verduras.

days.guide: Give the reading quiz; present the plate.

questions.q: Translate: 'Ice cream is bad for your health.'
questions.a: El helado es malo para la salud.

weeks.assessment_key: Reading quiz: comprehension questions on the article (e.g., which foods are good for health, how much water to drink). Oral plate presentation rubric (1–4): 6 sentences, names foods by group, uses 'Para mantener la salud debes…', adjective agreement, pronunciation.

weeks.prep: World map, photos of dishes, ingredients for guacamole (avocados, lime, onion, tomato, cilantro, salt) or tortilla española (potatoes, eggs, onion, olive oil). A market video (e.g., Mercado de Oaxaca or La Boquería in Barcelona).
misconceptions: Thinking 'tortilla' means the same everywhere. In Mexico it's a flat corn or flour bread; in Spain la tortilla española is a potato-and-egg omelet.
Assuming all Latin American food is spicy. Many dishes are mild; cuisine varies widely by country.

days.guide: Research one dish each from Mexico, Spain, Venezuela, Peru; add photos and captions.

questions.a: A round corn-flour flatbread from Venezuela (and Colombia), often split and filled.
Peru's dish of raw fish 'cooked'/cured in lime juice with onion and chile.

days.guide: Compare Mexican tortilla and tortilla española; write five sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'The Spanish tortilla has eggs and potatoes.'
questions.a: La tortilla española tiene huevos y papas (patatas in Spain).

days.guide: Watch a market video; list 10 foods in Spanish.

questions.a: The market.

days.guide: Prepare guacamole or tortilla española, narrating steps (Corto las papas, Mezclo los huevos…).

questions.a: Corto la cebolla.

days.guide: Write the cultural comparison reflection.

questions.a: A cold tomato-based vegetable soup from Spain (Andalusia).

weeks.assessment_key: Cultural comparison rubric (1–4): describes a family meal tradition and one studied tradition with specific details (food, when, who, meaning), makes 2+ comparisons (similarities and differences), uses some Spanish food vocabulary. Regional foods key: Mexico — tacos, mole, tamales; Spain — paella, gazpacho, tortilla española, churros; Venezuela — arepas (corn cakes), pabellón criollo; Peru — ceviche (raw fish cured in lime), lomo saltado.

weeks.prep: Paper or slides for a menu; play money in pesos or euros.
misconceptions: Ordering with 'Quiero' only. 'Quisiera…' (I would like) is more polite.
Forgetting agreement in menu descriptions: 'una ensalada fresca', 'unos tacos deliciosos'.

days.guide: Design a 12-item bilingual menu with prices.

questions.a: treinta y cinco pesos.

days.guide: Write a description for each item.

questions.a: Tacos de pollo deliciosos.

days.guide: Learn ¿Qué quieres comer? / Quisiera… / ¿Cuánto cuesta? / La cuenta, por favor.

questions.q: Order a sandwich and water politely.
questions.a: Quisiera un sándwich y un agua, por favor.

days.guide: Run the café role-play.

questions.a: La cuenta, por favor.

days.guide: Give the unit 6 test.

questions.q: Write: 'We always drink water at lunch.'
questions.a: Siempre bebemos agua en el almuerzo.

weeks.assessment_key: Menu project rubric (1–4): 12 items in categories, prices, a Spanish description per item with correct adjective agreement, attractive layout; role-play uses ¿Qué quieres comer/beber?, Quisiera…, ¿Cuánto cuesta?, La cuenta, por favor, numbers for prices. Unit 6 test: food listening, -er/-ir conjugations, short writing on eating habits (e.g., 'En el desayuno como cereal y bebo leche. Nunca como…').

weeks.prep: Family photos for a collage. A fictional family tree (find one in a Spanish textbook site or draw one). Vocabulary: el padre, la madre, los padres, el hermano, la hermana, el abuelo, la abuela, el tío, la tía, el primo, la prima, el hijo, la hija, el padrastro, la madrastra, el hermanastro, la hermanastra, el esposo, la esposa, la mascota.
misconceptions: Thinking 'los padres' means only fathers. It means parents (masculine plural covers mixed groups).
Using 'es' + possessive with family incorrectly. 'Es la madre de Juan' (She is Juan's mother) — Spanish uses 'de' for possession.

days.guide: Learn 20 family words; label a photo collage.

questions.a: mis abuelos.

days.guide: Read the fictional family tree; answer 10 ¿Quién es…? questions.

questions.q: If Ana is María's mother's sister, who is Ana to María?
questions.a: Ana es la tía de María.

days.guide: Write six sentences describing family members.

questions.q: Write: 'My brother is tall and funny.'
questions.a: Mi hermano es alto y gracioso.

days.guide: Add pets; make a short video tour.

questions.q: Write: 'My dog is small and lazy.'
questions.a: Mi perro es pequeño y perezoso.

days.guide: Give the family vocabulary quiz.

questions.a: The (male) cousin.

weeks.assessment_key: Family vocabulary quiz key samples: father → el padre; aunt → la tía; cousins (mixed) → los primos; grandparents → los abuelos; stepfather → el padrastro; half/step-sister → la medio hermana/la hermanastra; pet → la mascota. Family tree questions: answers use '___ es el/la ___ de ___.' 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Conjuguemos tener practice.
misconceptions: Using ser for age. Spanish uses tener: Tengo doce años.
Using 'su' only for 'his.' Su/sus can mean his, her, its, your (usted/ustedes) or their; context clarifies.

days.guide: Teach tener forms; Conjuguemos drill.

questions.q: Conjugate tener for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: tengo; tenemos.
tienen.

days.guide: Ask and answer ¿Cuántos años tiene…? for 10 people.

questions.a: Mi abuelo tiene setenta años.

days.guide: Teach possessive adjectives; 20-item practice.

questions.a: nuestras primas.
sus hermanos.

days.guide: Discuss family: siblings, cousins, pets, older/younger (mayor/menor).

questions.a: Tengo una hermana menor.

days.guide: Give the tener and possessives quiz.

questions.a: ¿Tienes mascotas?

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: tener — tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. Possessives: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/a/os/as, vuestro/a/os/as, su/sus. Samples: (our) house → nuestra casa; (my) cousins → mis primos; (their) dog → su perro; (your, tú) sisters → tus hermanas; How old is your grandma? → ¿Cuántos años tiene tu abuela? 80% passing.

weeks.prep: Pictures for captioning (someone shivering, eating, sleepy, scared, running late). Recording of 'Las mañanitas.' Read about the quinceañera.
misconceptions: Translating 'I am hungry' with estar or ser. Spanish uses tener: Tengo hambre.
Saying 'Tengo mucho frío' is right, but 'Tengo muy frío' is wrong — tener expressions use mucho/mucha (nouns).

days.guide: Learn 8 expressions; caption 10 pictures.

questions.q: Caption a picture of a boy shivering.
questions.a: Él tiene frío.
Tengo mucha hambre.

days.guide: Write a to-do list with tener que + infinitive.

questions.q: Write: 'My brother has to clean his room.'
questions.a: Mi hermano tiene que limpiar su cuarto.

days.guide: Read about the quinceañera and las mañanitas; listen and note five words.

questions.a: A celebration of a girl's 15th birthday marking her passage to young womanhood, often with a Mass, a formal dress, a waltz and a party.
On birthdays (and saints' days), often early in the morning, in Mexico.

days.guide: Describe a family party in present tense.

questions.q: Write: 'At the party we eat cake.'
questions.a: En la fiesta comemos pastel.

days.guide: Give the quiz with listening.

questions.q: Which expression: 'Tienes ___' when you are right?
questions.a: Tienes razón.

weeks.assessment_key: Tener expressions quiz key: tener hambre (to be hungry), sed (thirsty), frío (cold), calor (hot), sueño (sleepy), miedo (afraid), prisa (in a hurry), razón (right), ___ años (to be __ years old); tener que + infinitive (to have to). Samples: 'We are very thirsty' → Tenemos mucha sed; 'I have to study' → Tengo que estudiar; 'She is afraid' → Ella tiene miedo. Listening: identify expression from a short audio description. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Poster board, family photos, index cards, phone to record.
misconceptions: Thinking the second surname is a middle name. In Spanish naming, the first surname is the father's first surname and the second is the mother's first surname.
Reading the full script. Use key-word index cards.

days.guide: Explain double surnames; write your name in that format.

questions.q: If a father is Juan López Ruiz and the mother is Ana Pérez Gómez, what are their child's surnames?
questions.a: López Pérez (father's first surname + mother's first surname).

days.guide: Build the tree with 12+ relatives, labels and ages.

questions.a: On the mother's side (maternal).

days.guide: Write a 10–12 sentence presentation.

questions.q: Write: 'My aunt is 40 years old and she likes to read.'
questions.a: Mi tía tiene cuarenta años y le gusta leer.

days.guide: Rehearse with key-word cards; record.

questions.a: Estos son mis abuelos paternos.

days.guide: Present and give the unit 7 test.

questions.a: casado/casada.

weeks.assessment_key: Family tree presentation rubric (1–4 each): content (12+ relatives with relationships and ages), language (tener, ser, possessives, gustar; agreement), fluency/pronunciation (2 minutes with notes), visual (labels in Spanish). Unit 7 test: family vocabulary, tener and tener expressions, possessives, ages. Surname example: Gabriel García Márquez → father's surname García, mother's surname Márquez.

weeks.prep: Stuffed animal, household objects. Prepositions: encima de, debajo de, al lado de, delante de, detrás de, cerca de, lejos de, entre, dentro de, a la derecha de, a la izquierda de.
misconceptions: Using ser for location. Location of things and people uses estar: El libro está en la mesa (events use ser: La fiesta es en mi casa).
Forgetting de + el = del: al lado del sofá.

days.guide: Teach estar forms and uses (location, feelings).

questions.q: Conjugate estar for tú and ellos.
questions.a: estás; están.
Estoy cansado.

days.guide: Place a stuffed animal in 12 spots and describe.

questions.q: Say: 'The bear is behind the chair.'
questions.a: El oso está detrás de la silla.

questions.q: Say: 'The cat is on top of the bed.'
questions.a: El gato está encima de la cama.

days.guide: Hide objects and give clues; switch roles.

questions.q: Give a clue: 'It's near the door.'
questions.a: Está cerca de la puerta.

days.guide: Sort 15 sentences into ser or estar and explain.

questions.a: es — origin.

questions.q: Choose: Mi madre (es/está) en la cocina.
questions.a: está — location.

days.guide: Give the estar and prepositions quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'The backpack is next to the sofa.'
questions.a: La mochila está al lado del sofá.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: estar — estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. Samples: The cat is under the table → El gato está debajo de la mesa; The books are next to the computer → Los libros están al lado de la computadora; We are near the park → Estamos cerca del parque. Ser vs estar sort: origin, description, profession, time → ser; location, feelings/conditions → estar. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Hand-drawn town map, Google Maps Street View of the Plaza de la Constitución/Zócalo in Oaxaca or the Plaza Mayor in Salamanca. Places: la biblioteca, el parque, el centro comercial, la iglesia, la plaza, el cine, el gimnasio, la playa, el restaurante, el supermercado, el banco, el museo, la escuela, el hospital, el correo, la piscina.
misconceptions: Saying 'el iglesia' because it starts with a vowel. It's la iglesia (feminine).
Thinking a plaza is like a mall. A Spanish/Latin American plaza is an open central square for gathering, often with a church and government buildings.

days.guide: Learn 16 places; label a neighborhood map.

questions.q: How do you say 'the library' and 'the mall'?
questions.a: la biblioteca; el centro comercial.

days.guide: Answer ¿Dónde está…? using map prepositions.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Dónde está el parque? (across from/in front of the school)
questions.a: El parque está delante de la escuela (or enfrente de la escuela).

days.guide: Read about the central plaza; compare with a California downtown.

questions.q: What buildings are usually around a main plaza?
questions.a: A church/cathedral, the town hall (ayuntamiento), shops and cafés.

days.guide: Virtual tour; write 8 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'In the plaza there is a church and many people.'
questions.a: En la plaza hay una iglesia y mucha gente.

days.guide: Give the places and map quiz.

questions.a: The movie theater.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: 16 places with articles; map section answers '¿Dónde está…?' with estar + preposition (e.g., La biblioteca está al lado del parque; El cine está entre el banco y el restaurante). Plaza culture: central square (plaza mayor/zócalo) surrounded by church, town hall, shops and cafés; center of social life, festivals and the paseo. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Weekly planner. Question words: ¿Qué?, ¿Quién?, ¿Dónde?, ¿Adónde?, ¿Cuándo?, ¿Con quién?, ¿Por qué?, ¿Cómo?, ¿Cuántos?
misconceptions: Saying 'a el parque.' a + el contracts to al: Voy al parque (a la is not contracted: Voy a la playa).
Using ¿Dónde? with ir. With motion use ¿Adónde vas?

days.guide: Teach ir forms and a + el = al.

questions.a: vamos.

questions.q: Complete: Mis padres van ___ (a + el) cine.
questions.a: al.

days.guide: Review question words; write 10 questions.

questions.q: Ask: 'Who do you go to the movies with?'
questions.a: ¿Con quién vas al cine?
¿Dónde? = where (location); ¿Adónde? = to where (destination with motion).

days.guide: Fill a planner; write 7 sentences.

questions.q: Write: 'On Saturdays I go to the gym.'
questions.a: Los sábados voy al gimnasio.

days.guide: Interview a family member; write a report.

questions.q: Report: 'My mom goes to the supermarket on Fridays.'
questions.a: Mi mamá va al supermercado los viernes.

days.guide: Give the ir and question words quiz.

questions.a: Mañana voy a la biblioteca.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz key: ir — voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Samples: I go to the park → Voy al parque; We go to the beach on weekends → Vamos a la playa los fines de semana; Where are you going? → ¿Adónde vas?; With whom do you go? → ¿Con quién vas? Question words matching. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: A printed map of a Spanish city center (e.g., Madrid's Puerta del Sol area or a textbook map). Record or prepare directions to read aloud.
misconceptions: Confusing derecho (straight) and derecha (right).
Forgetting to use the tú command forms as chunks: dobla, sigue, cruza.

days.guide: Learn direction words; follow your spoken directions around the house.

questions.a: Go straight ahead.
Dobla a la izquierda.

days.guide: Trace routes on a city map as you read directions.

questions.a: Walk three blocks.

days.guide: Write directions to three local places.

questions.q: Write: 'Turn right on the corner and walk two blocks.'
questions.a: Dobla a la derecha en la esquina y camina dos cuadras.

days.guide: Information-gap game.

questions.q: Ask: 'Excuse me, where is the museum?'
questions.a: Perdón, ¿dónde está el museo?

days.guide: Give the direction-following listening quiz.

questions.a: Cross the street.

weeks.assessment_key: Listening quiz: child follows 5 sets of directions on a map and names the destination (5/5 proficient, 4/5 acceptable). Key phrases: dobla a la derecha (turn right), dobla a la izquierda (turn left), sigue todo derecho (go straight), cruza la calle (cross the street), camina dos cuadras (walk two blocks), en la esquina (on the corner).

weeks.prep: Phone/camera, town map, a short tourist brochure in Spanish (many city tourism sites have Spanish versions).
misconceptions: Narrating with only 'hay.' Vary: está, la gente va, me gusta, se puede…
Forgetting the tourist role uses usted with strangers: ¿Puede usted ayudarme?

days.guide: Choose five places; write two sentences each.

questions.q: Write: 'The park is near my house. People go to the park to walk.'
questions.a: El parque está cerca de mi casa. La gente va al parque para caminar.

days.guide: Film and narrate a 2-minute tour.

questions.a: Este es el supermercado.

days.guide: Read a tourist brochure; answer questions.

questions.a: City hall.

days.guide: Role-play a tourist asking directions (usted).

questions.q: Ask politely: 'Where is the plaza, please?'
questions.a: Perdone, ¿dónde está la plaza, por favor?

days.guide: Give the unit 8 test.

questions.q: Translate: 'We are going to the museum.'
questions.a: Vamos al museo.

weeks.assessment_key: Town tour video rubric (1–4 each): 5 places with location (estar + prepositions) and activities, 2 minutes, pronunciation, visuals. Unit 8 test: estar conjugation and location, ir conjugation and al/a la, places vocabulary, directions. Model: 'Esta es la biblioteca. Está al lado del parque. La gente va a la biblioteca para leer.'

weeks.prep: Sports schedule; read about Real Madrid–Barcelona (El Clásico) or Boca Juniors–River Plate (Superclásico). Sports: el fútbol, el béisbol, el básquetbol, el vóleibol, el tenis, el fútbol americano, el golf, el hockey, la natación, el ciclismo, el atletismo, el boliche.
misconceptions: Forgetting 'a' in ir a + infinitive: 'Voy jugar.' Say Voy a jugar.
Saying 'jugar fútbol' is common in Latin America, but jugar al fútbol is standard; accept both and note jugar a + el = al.

days.guide: Learn 12 sports with jugar a; describe who plays what.

questions.a: Mi hermana juega al fútbol.

questions.q: Conjugate jugar for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: juego; jugamos.

days.guide: Teach ir a + infinitive; write 10 sentences about next weekend.

questions.q: Write: 'I'm going to read a book this weekend.'
questions.a: Voy a leer un libro este fin de semana.

days.guide: Read about a rivalry; summarize in five Spanish sentences.

questions.a: The famous soccer match between Real Madrid and FC Barcelona.

days.guide: Make a two-week plans calendar; tell a parent your plans.

questions.q: Say: 'Tomorrow I'm going to go to the park.'
questions.a: Mañana voy a ir al parque.

days.guide: Give the ir a + infinitive quiz.

questions.q: Translate: 'What are you going to do tonight?'
questions.a: ¿Qué vas a hacer esta noche?

weeks.assessment_key: Ir a + infinitive quiz samples: 'I'm going to play basketball' → Voy a jugar al básquetbol; 'We are going to watch the game tonight' → Vamos a ver el partido esta noche; 'Are you going to swim tomorrow?' → ¿Vas a nadar mañana?; 'They are going to visit grandma next weekend' → Van a visitar a la abuela el próximo fin de semana. 80% proficient.

weeks.prep: Phone for texting/calling practice. Read about punctuality norms (e.g., social events often start later than the stated time in much of Latin America and Spain; business meetings expect punctuality).
misconceptions: Declining without a reason. Polite decline: Lo siento, no puedo. Tengo que…
Overgeneralizing 'everyone is always late' as a stereotype. Norms vary by country, setting and person.

days.guide: Practice invitation chunks in pairs.

questions.q: Invite a friend to the movies Saturday.
questions.a: ¿Quieres ir al cine el sábado?

questions.q: Decline because you have to study.
questions.a: Lo siento, no puedo. Tengo que estudiar.

days.guide: Write a text exchange with time and place.

questions.a: ¿A qué hora? — A las cuatro.

days.guide: Simulated phone call; respond to an excuse.

questions.q: Your friend says she's busy. React sympathetically.
questions.a: ¡Qué pena! Otro día, entonces.

days.guide: Read and discuss punctuality and social plans.

questions.q: Name one cultural difference in social plans you read about.
questions.a: Example: in Spain dinner and social events often start much later (9–10 p.m.); friends may arrive after the stated time for informal parties.

days.guide: Record an unscripted invitation conversation.

questions.a: ¡Claro que sí! ¡Me encantaría!

weeks.assessment_key: Interpersonal invitation rubric (1–4): invites with ¿Quieres ir…? including place and time, accepts (¡Claro que sí! / ¡Qué bueno!) or declines (Lo siento, no puedo, tengo que… / Estoy ocupado/a), asks ¿A qué hora? / ¿Dónde?, reacts (¡Qué pena!), keeps the conversation going naturally.

weeks.prep: All unit tests, flashcards, Conjuguemos, three short texts (menu, family profile, town brochure).
misconceptions: Mixing up ser and estar under pressure. Remember: ser = origin, description, identity; estar = location and feelings.
Forgetting verb endings by type. Review -ar, -er, -ir charts side by side.

days.guide: Review units 1–5 with a practice test.

questions.q: Translate: 'Today is Friday, it's 10:30 and it's sunny.'
questions.a: Hoy es viernes, son las diez y media y hace sol.

days.guide: Review units 6–9 with Conjuguemos drills.

questions.q: Conjugate vivir, tener and ir for nosotros.
questions.a: vivimos, tenemos, vamos.

days.guide: Read three short texts; answer questions.

questions.q: On a menu, what is 'el postre'?
questions.a: Dessert.

days.guide: Mock 3-minute interview on all topics.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
questions.a: Voy a ___ (infinitive), e.g., Voy a jugar al fútbol con mis amigos.

days.guide: Write a practice paragraph about yourself, family and weekend plans.

questions.q: Write: 'I have two brothers and we live in California.'
questions.a: Tengo dos hermanos y vivimos en California.

weeks.assessment_key: Self-scored practice test: student checks answers with the unit keys (greetings, calendar, ser/adjectives, gustar, school, -ar/-er/-ir, food, family/tener, estar, ir, ir a + infinitive). Goal 80%+; any section under 80% gets a targeted review. Writing practice: paragraph with 8+ sentences using at least 5 different verbs correctly.

weeks.prep: Final exam packet: an authentic short text (pen-pal profile or town website page) and a short audio (e.g., a Spanish Proficiency Exercises clip) with comprehension questions you write in advance. Can-do checklist.
misconceptions: Translating every word in a reading. Use cognates, context and key words for the gist.
Memorizing a speech for the interpersonal part. Listen and respond to the actual questions.

days.guide: Read the authentic text and listen to the audio; answer questions.

questions.q: What strategy helps with unknown words?
questions.a: Look for cognates (e.g., 'familia,' 'música'), use context and pictures, and focus on main ideas.

days.guide: Hold a 4-minute conversation on all topics.

questions.q: Answer: ¿Qué te gusta comer y qué no te gusta?
questions.a: Me gusta(n) ___ pero no me gusta(n) ___ (with correct gusta/gustan).

days.guide: Write and present 'Mi vida' (12–15 sentences).

questions.a: Example: Hola, me llamo ___, tengo ___ años y soy de ___.

days.guide: Present one cultural comparison from the year.

questions.a: Example: En España la gente se saluda con dos besos, pero en mi familia damos abrazos.

days.guide: Complete the can-do self-assessment; set goals for Spanish 1B.

questions.q: Write one can-do statement you've mastered.
questions.a: Example: 'I can introduce myself and describe my family.'

weeks.assessment_key: Integrated performance assessment rubric (1–4 each mode): Interpretive — identifies main idea and 4+ key details from text and audio; Interpersonal — 4-minute conversation, answers and asks questions on self, family, school, food, plans, uses sentences (Novice Mid), comprehensible; Presentational — 'Mi vida' 12–15 sentences covering greetings/identity, description (ser), likes (gustar), school, food, family (tener), town (estar/ir) and plans (ir a), with accurate agreement and verb forms; Cultures — accurate comparison with specific details. Proficient = 3s across.
